decks.module: Who must be licensed, exemptions and denials

cards.front: Who must hold a West Virginia driver's license, and what must they carry while driving?
cards.back: Anyone who lives in West Virginia and wants to drive a motor vehicle on public roads must hold a West Virginia driver's license unless expressly exempt, and must carry that license while driving.

cards.front: Who is exempt from the license requirement while on military duty?
cards.back: A person operating a motor vehicle in the armed services of the United States while performing official duties is exempt from the West Virginia license requirement.

cards.front: Which nonresident drivers are exempt, and for how long each year?
cards.back: A nonresident who is at least sixteen years old and holds a valid license from another state or country is exempt from needing a West Virginia license, but only for ninety days in a calendar year.

cards.front: Which college students are exempt from needing a West Virginia license?
cards.back: A nonresident attending a West Virginia college or university who holds a valid license from another state is exempt from the West Virginia license requirement.

cards.front: Who can be denied a license because of alcohol or narcotic habits?
cards.back: A habitual user of alcoholic beverages or a person addicted to narcotic drugs can be denied a driver's license.

cards.front: When can a driver suspended or revoked in another jurisdiction be denied a license?
cards.back: A person whose driver's license has been suspended or revoked by West Virginia, another state or a foreign jurisdiction can be denied a license until that suspension or revocation period expires.

cards.front: Whom may the Commissioner deny a license as a hazard to the public?
cards.back: A license can be denied to anyone the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles has good cause to believe would endanger public safety or welfare when operating a motor vehicle.

cards.front: Which applicants under eighteen can be denied a license?
cards.back: A person under the age of eighteen who is neither enrolled in nor graduated from an approved educational institution can be denied a driver's license.

cards.front: Which nonresident exemption carries the ninety-day limit?
cards.back: The ninety-day calendar-year limit attaches to the general exemption for nonresident drivers at least sixteen years old with a valid out-of-state license, not to the separate exemption for nonresident college students.
cards.memory_hook: Which exemption has a day limit

decks.module: Core document set for first-time applicants

cards.front: Which four kinds of proof must a first-time applicant bring, and what happens to the documents?
cards.back: Every first-time license applicant must bring documents proving identity, Social Security number, any legal name change that has ever occurred, and West Virginia residency, and the DMV scans the documents securely and returns them.

cards.front: What must new, transfer and expired-license applicants provide?
cards.back: New, transfer and expired-license applicants must provide one proof of identity, their Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency showing name and physical address, and proof of legal name change if the name differs from the identity document.

cards.front: Who does the handbook treat as a first-time applicant?
cards.back: The handbook treats as a first-time applicant anyone who has never held a driver's license or ID card, who is transferring an out-of-state license, or whose West Virginia license has been expired for more than three years.

cards.front: How many identity proofs do you present, and why must your name match Social Security records?
cards.back: You must present exactly one proof of identity and must provide your Social Security number, and your full legal name must match the name on file with the Social Security Administration because the DMV checks every number with that agency.

cards.front: What must a first-time applicant for a permit, license or ID provide?
cards.back: A first-time applicant for an instruction permit, driver's license or identification card must provide a Social Security number, one proof of identity, two proofs of West Virginia residency and the application form the DMV provides, plus name-change documents such as a certified marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order when the name has changed.

cards.front: What are the two kinds of license or ID card, and what decides the documents you bring?
cards.back: West Virginia offers two kinds of driver's license and ID card, a Not For Federal Use card and a REAL ID or For Federal Use card with a gold star, and the documents you must bring depend on which type you choose.

cards.front: When does an expired West Virginia or out-of-state license force a retest?
cards.back: A West Virginia license expired three years or more sends the holder through the full examination process as a first-time applicant, and an expired out-of-state license also requires retesting.

decks.module: Identity, Social Security and name-change proofs

cards.front: Which birth certificates prove identity, and which do not?
cards.back: An original or certified copy of a United States birth certificate proves identity, including State Department and military birth certificates, but hospital birth certificates and Bureau of Census records are not acceptable.

cards.front: Which passport documents prove identity?
cards.back: A valid United States passport or passport card is an acceptable proof of identity.

cards.front: How may a foreign-born applicant prove identity?
cards.back: A foreign-born applicant may prove identity with a valid, unexpired Department of Homeland Security document such as a Permanent Resident Card, an employment authorization document, a certificate of naturalization or citizenship, a consular report of birth abroad, or a foreign passport carrying a valid United States visa with the approved arrival record of the most recent admittance.

cards.front: What happens if your name or birth date does not match Social Security records?
cards.back: If your name or date of birth does not match Social Security Administration records, the problem must be corrected before an instruction permit, license or identification card can be issued.

cards.front: What must an applicant not eligible for a Social Security number submit?
cards.back: An applicant who is not eligible for a Social Security number must submit a letter from the Social Security Administration stating that ineligibility.

cards.front: Which documents prove your Social Security number, and which copy is not acceptable?
cards.back: Acceptable proof of Social Security number is the original card in your current legal name, an original Wage and Tax Statement or a payroll stub showing the employer's name and identification number along with your name, address and number, or a ten ninety-nine form showing your full number and name, and a photocopy of the Wage and Tax Statement is not acceptable.

cards.front: When is proof of legal name change required, and why?
cards.back: Proof of legal name change is required if your name has ever changed, because the DMV must be able to link every legal name you have used.

cards.front: Which documents prove a legal name change, and which are rejected?
cards.back: Acceptable proof of a legal name change is a marriage certificate for each marriage if married more than once, an amended birth certificate, a court order or a divorce decree showing the legal name, while souvenir marriage documents and minister's copies are not acceptable.

cards.front: Which birth certificates prove identity and which are rejected?
cards.back: State Department and military birth certificates count as proof of identity, while hospital birth certificates and Bureau of Census records do not.

cards.front: How can a Wage and Tax Statement serve two purposes, and what copy fails?
cards.back: An original Wage and Tax Statement proves the Social Security number and may also serve as one residency proof if it is not more than eighteen months old, but a photocopy of it is not acceptable.

cards.front: What rules govern the two residency proofs, including age and post office boxes?
cards.back: Two proofs of West Virginia residency are required, documents showing a post office box are not acceptable, any recurring document such as a utility bill cannot be more than ninety days old, and a married applicant may use documents in the spouse's name together with a marriage certificate.

cards.front: Which everyday documents count as proof of West Virginia residency?
cards.back: Residency proofs include a West Virginia utility bill that is not a termination notice, tax records with a West Virginia street address, mortgage or homeowner insurance documents, a voter registration card, a vehicle registration card, a bank statement, a rental or lease agreement, an auto insurance card, a hunting license and a paycheck stub from a West Virginia employer showing a current physical address that is not handwritten.

cards.front: Which letters and statements also count as proof of residency?
cards.back: Further residency proofs include a college admissions letter showing in-state residency, a nine one one address letter, a Social Security benefits letter, a Post Office letter assigning a new physical West Virginia address, a Wage and Tax Statement not more than eighteen months old, and a letter from a shelter, hotel, nursing home or similar facility giving its physical address and stating that the applicant lives there.

cards.front: Why will the DMV refuse an applicant without a West Virginia physical address?
cards.back: An applicant for any driver's license or identification card must be a West Virginia resident, and the DMV will not license or issue a card to anyone who does not give a West Virginia physical address.

cards.front: May a former West Virginia resident living elsewhere renew a West Virginia card?
cards.back: A former West Virginia resident who now lives elsewhere may not renew a West Virginia license or identification card until residency in the state is established again.

cards.front: When must a renewing driver bring residency documents again?
cards.back: Once a new resident's two residency documents have been scanned into the record, later renewals or transactions require two residency documents again only if the physical address has changed.

cards.front: Which residency documents have a ninety-day limit and which an eighteen-month limit?
cards.back: A recurring residency document such as a utility bill may be no more than ninety days old, whereas a Wage and Tax Statement used as residency proof may be up to eighteen months old.

cards.front: Which post office document is rejected and which is accepted as residency proof?
cards.back: A document showing a post office box is rejected as residency proof, while a letter from the Post Office assigning the applicant a new physical West Virginia address is accepted.
cards.memory_hook: Box address versus Post Office letter

decks.module: New residents, transfers and expired licenses

cards.front: What extra document must an applicant transferring from another state present?
cards.back: An applicant transferring a license from another state must also hand in the current out-of-state license or present a certified driving record from that state dated thirty days or less before the application.

cards.front: What must a new resident do to transfer a valid out-of-state license?
cards.back: A new resident with a valid, unexpired out-of-state license may transfer it after passing a vision screening, completing a brief alcohol awareness course and surrendering the out-of-state license, and must present every document required of a first-time applicant.

cards.front: How soon must a new resident apply, and what happens to a motorcycle endorsement?
cards.back: New residents who want to drive in West Virginia must apply for a West Virginia license within thirty days of establishing residency, and a motorcycle endorsement on the old license transfers for an additional fee.

cards.front: When must a new resident take all first-time examinations or obtain a driving record?
cards.back: If the out-of-state license has been expired for more than three years, the new resident must take every examination required of a first-time applicant, and a new resident who cannot produce the out-of-state license must obtain a certified driving record from the former state to waive testing.

cards.front: What happens when a new resident's out-of-state license is suspended or revoked?
cards.back: A new resident whose out-of-state license is suspended or revoked will not be licensed in West Virginia until the Problem Driver Point System issues a clearance, and driving in the state on a license suspended or revoked anywhere is illegal.

cards.front: When does an expired license require a full retest?
cards.back: Anyone renewing a West Virginia license, including a commercial driver's license, that has been expired for three years or more must retest through the full examination process with all first-time documents, and an expired out-of-state license also requires retesting.

cards.front: When and why did West Virginia adopt the REAL ID Act standards?
cards.back: In twenty eleven West Virginia adopted the federal licensing standards of the REAL ID Act of two thousand five, a secure license and identification card program meant to improve the integrity and security of all driver's licenses and ID cards nationwide.

cards.front: Which deadline is thirty days and which is twenty days?
cards.back: New residents have thirty days after establishing residency to apply for a West Virginia license, while an in-state address change must be reported to the DMV in writing within twenty days.

cards.front: When does a transfer waive testing, and when does it not?
cards.back: A transfer applicant who presents a valid out-of-state license, or a certified driving record when that license cannot be produced, waives the testing requirement, but an out-of-state license expired more than three years brings every first-time examination.

cards.front: What is the Problem Driver Point System, and who is reviewed through it?
cards.back: Every license applicant and every renewing driver is reviewed through the Problem Driver Point System, a national driver registry that tracks violations and suspensions from state to state.

cards.front: Why must out-of-state citations and suspensions be settled before applying?
cards.back: The DMV is prohibited from licensing a driver whose record shows an unsettled problem in another state or jurisdiction, so pending citations and suspensions elsewhere must be satisfied before applying for or renewing a West Virginia license.

cards.front: How does the DMV handle notice of an unpaid citation from another state?
cards.back: When another state reports an unpaid citation, the West Virginia DMV notifies the driver by certified mail at the address in its system, allows a certain amount of time to resolve it, and then suspends the license, and the driver must supply proof of payment or of satisfying the court order before reinstatement.

cards.front: Who must prove an unpaid citation was resolved, and will the court tell the DMV?
cards.back: Unpaid citations remain the driver's own responsibility, and the court should not be expected to notify the DMV when an unpaid citation is resolved.

cards.front: How soon must an address change be reported, and does telling the Post Office count?
cards.back: A driver who changes address must notify the DMV in writing within twenty days, failure to do so can bring a fine or imprisonment, and telling only the Post Office does not update the DMV record or forward DMV mail.
cards.memory_hook: Twenty days to report address change

cards.front: What steps precede a suspension for an unpaid out-of-state citation, and what restores the license?
cards.back: A suspension for an unpaid out-of-state citation follows certified-mail notice and a period to respond, and reinstatement requires the driver's own proof of payment because the court will not notify the DMV.

decks.module: Card types, mailing and color coding

cards.front: What does a gold star on a license or ID card mean?
cards.back: A license or ID card certified as REAL ID compliant carries a gold star on its face showing that it meets full federal requirements for use at airports and other designated federal facilities across the country.

cards.front: How does a new license reach the applicant, and what covers the wait?
cards.back: A license applied for at any DMV location arrives at the applicant's address by mail in approximately fifteen to twenty business days, and a temporary license issued when the application is accepted covers the production and shipping time.

cards.front: What does a renewal applicant for a Not For Federal Use card bring if nothing or something changed?
cards.back: A renewal applicant for a Not For Federal Use card with no changes brings only the current license or ID card and the renewal application, while an address change requires two proofs of West Virginia residency and a legal name change requires proof of that change.

cards.front: How do you replace a lost, stolen or destroyed license, and what proofs may be needed?
cards.back: If a driver's license is lost, stolen or destroyed, a duplicate can be requested online or at a Regional Office, with proof of any legal name change and two residency proofs if the address changed since the last card.

cards.front: What must a For Federal Use renewal or duplicate applicant provide?
cards.back: A For Federal Use renewal or duplicate applicant must provide one proof of identity, a Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency with name and physical address, and proof of legal name change if the name has ever changed.

cards.front: How much extra does the For Federal Use card cost, and how is it delivered?
cards.back: The For Federal Use card costs an additional ten dollars and is mailed to the applicant in fifteen to twenty business days, with a temporary license issued when the application is accepted.

cards.front: What must you present for a duplicate license, and what applies to non-citizens?
cards.back: To obtain a duplicate license you present two residency documents if your address changed and evidence of any name change, you must supply your Social Security number if it is missing or wrong in the DMV database, and a non-citizen must present the documents that verify legal status, identity and residency.

cards.front: How are licenses color-coded by age?
cards.back: Applicants aged fifteen to seventeen receive a vertical license or instruction permit color-coded red, applicants aged eighteen to twenty receive a vertical card color-coded blue, and applicants twenty-one or older receive a horizontal license with a landscape background.

cards.front: How do renewal documents differ between the two card types?
cards.back: A For Federal Use renewal needs the full document set of identity proof, Social Security number, two residency proofs and any name-change proof, whereas a Not For Federal Use renewal with no changes needs only the current card and the renewal application.

cards.front: Which license colors and shapes go with which ages?
cards.back: Red color coding marks license holders aged fifteen to seventeen and blue marks those aged eighteen to twenty, both on vertical cards, while a horizontal landscape card marks age twenty-one or older.

cards.front: What documents must an immigrant applicant provide?
cards.back: An immigrant applying for a permit, license or identification card provides a Social Security number, two proofs of West Virginia residency, and one of a Permanent Resident Card, a valid temporary resident stamp in a foreign passport with English translation or on the arrival record, or a valid re-entry permit.

cards.front: What documents must a non-immigrant applicant provide?
cards.back: A non-immigrant applicant provides a Social Security number or a Social Security Administration denial letter, two residency proofs, a valid foreign passport, the federal arrival record, a visa when the applicant's nation requires one, original documents verifying status and authorized stay, and written school verification for student statuses or employer verification for work statuses.

cards.front: What documents must a refugee applicant provide?
cards.back: A refugee applicant provides a Social Security number or denial letter, two residency proofs, an arrival record showing the grant of refugee status, a Reception and Placement Program Assurance form, and written verification of identity and residency from an employee of a State Department approved sponsoring organization.

cards.front: What must a refugee without a sponsor or an asylum seeker provide?
cards.back: A refugee without an approved sponsoring organization, or a person seeking asylum, provides two residency proofs, a Social Security number or denial letter, an arrival record stamped as refugee or asylee, and employment authorization documents.

cards.front: Which applicant groups may substitute a Social Security denial letter?
cards.back: Non-immigrant and refugee applicants may substitute a Social Security Administration denial letter for a Social Security number, while the immigrant document list on the same page names only the Social Security number.
